title: Internet Control Message Protocol

hero.subtitle: The error-reporting and diagnostic protocol that keeps the Internet running

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
The Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) is used by network devices to send error messages and operational information. It is an integral part of the Internet Protocol suite, operating at the network layer alongside IP.

ICMP messages are encapsulated inside IP datagrams (protocol number 1). Though ICMP uses IP for delivery, it is considered part of the IP layer, not a transport protocol.

ICMP serves two primary purposes: error reporting (e.g., destination unreachable) and diagnostics (e.g., ping and traceroute).
sections.plainLanguage: The Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) lets network devices send error messages and operational information. ICMP messages travel inside IP datagrams but belong to the IP layer. It serves two purposes: error reporting, such as destination unreachable, and diagnostics, such as ping and traceroute.

sections.title: Message Types
sections.content:
ICMP messages are identified by a Type field and further refined by a Code field:

0Echo Reply — Response to a ping request
3Destination Unreachable — Packet could not be delivered
5Redirect — Better route available
8Echo Request — Ping request
11Time Exceeded — TTL expired in transit
12Parameter Problem — Bad IP header
sections.plainLanguage: Each ICMP message has a Type field that says what kind it is and a Code field that adds detail. Examples are 8 (Echo Request), 0 (Echo Reply), 3 (Destination Unreachable), 5 (Redirect), 11 (Time Exceeded) and 12 (Parameter Problem).

sections.title: Echo Request/Reply
sections.content:
The Echo Request (Type 8) and Echo Reply (Type 0) messages are the basis of the ping utility, one of the most widely used network diagnostic tools.

Ping Example
$ ping 198.51.100.1
PING 198.51.100.1: 56 data bytes
64 bytes from 198.51.100.1: icmp_seq=0 ttl=64 time=1.234 ms
64 bytes from 198.51.100.1: icmp_seq=1 ttl=64 time=1.156 ms
64 bytes from 198.51.100.1: icmp_seq=2 ttl=64 time=1.089 ms
sections.plainLanguage: Ping works by sending an Echo Request (Type 8) and waiting for an Echo Reply (Type 0). The reply shows that the other host is reachable, and the response time can be measured.

sections.title: Error Reporting
sections.content:
When a router or destination host encounters a problem delivering a packet, it generates an ICMP error message and sends it back to the source.

Destination Unreachable (Type 3)
Sent when a packet cannot reach its destination. Code values distinguish: 0=Network Unreachable, 1=Host Unreachable, 3=Port Unreachable, 4=Fragmentation Needed but DF set.
Time Exceeded (Type 11)
Sent when a packet's TTL reaches zero (Code 0) or when fragment reassembly times out (Code 1). This is the basis of the traceroute utility.
Redirect (Type 5)
Sent by a router to inform a host that a better next-hop router exists for a particular destination.

ICMP error messages must never be generated in response to other ICMP error messages, to prevent infinite loops. RFC 1122 adds that they must not be sent in response to broadcast or multicast datagrams.
sections.plainLanguage: When a router or host cannot deliver a packet, it sends an ICMP error message to the source. Destination Unreachable says delivery failed, Time Exceeded says the TTL reached zero, and Redirect says a better next-hop router exists. ICMP errors are never sent in response to other ICMP errors, to prevent endless loops.

sections.title: Usage
sections.content:
ICMP is essential to several widely-used network diagnostic tools:

Tool
ICMP Types Used
Purpose
ping
Type 8 / Type 0
Test reachability and measure RTT
traceroute
Type 11 / Type 3
Map the path packets take
Path MTU Discovery
Type 3, Code 4
Find largest packet size for a path

Many firewalls filter ICMP traffic for security reasons. While blocking unnecessary types is reasonable, blocking all ICMP can break Path MTU Discovery and make debugging difficult.
sections.plainLanguage: Ping uses Echo messages (Types 8 and 0). Traceroute uses Time Exceeded and Destination Unreachable (Types 11 and 3). Path MTU Discovery uses Type 3, Code 4. Blocking all ICMP in a firewall can break Path MTU Discovery and make debugging harder.

references.text: Braden, R., "Requirements for Internet Hosts -- Communication Layers", RFC 1122, October 1989.

subtitle: The error-reporting and diagnostic protocol that keeps the Internet running

plainLanguage.summary: ICMP carries error reports and diagnostic messages between hosts and routers. It tells a sender when a packet could not be delivered or timed out, and it supports ping and traceroute.

questions: what is icmp type 3 destination unreachable
what is an icmp echo request

tldr.problem: IP is connectionless, so a gateway or host that drops or cannot deliver a datagram has no way to tell the sender why.
tldr.mechanism: The gateway or host sends an ICMP message, carried in an IP datagram with protocol number 1, back to the source. It carries a Type, a Code, a checksum and, for errors, the original IP header plus the first 64 bits of its data.
tldr.outcome: ICMP reports problems but does not make IP reliable. It still underpins ping, traceroute and path MTU discovery.

today: ICMP is still essential. Ping and traceroute rely on it, and IPv6 has its own version, ICMPv6, which is required for the protocol to work at all. Some types in this RFC, such as Source Quench (4), have since been deprecated. Many firewalls filter ICMP, and blocking too much can break path MTU discovery.

fields.name: Type
fields.desc: Identifies the message: 0 Echo Reply, 3 Destination Unreachable, 4 Source Quench, 5 Redirect, 8 Echo, 11 Time Exceeded, 12 Parameter Problem, 13/14 Timestamp, 15/16 Information.

fields.name: Code
fields.desc: Refines the Type, for example the reason a destination was unreachable.

fields.name: Checksum
fields.desc: 16-bit one's complement of the one's complement sum of the ICMP message starting with the Type, computed with the field as zero.

fields.name: Type-specific
fields.desc: Depends on the type. Unused (must be zero) in Destination Unreachable and Time Exceeded, which are followed by the original Internet Header + 64 bits of data.

fields.name: Type
fields.desc: 8 for echo message, 0 for echo reply message.

fields.name: Checksum
fields.desc: One's complement checksum of the ICMP message, recomputed for the reply.

fields.name: Identifier
fields.desc: Aids in matching echos and replies. May be zero. Like a port: it can identify a session.

fields.name: Sequence Number
fields.desc: Aids in matching echos and replies. May be zero. Can be incremented on each echo request sent.

messages.label: Echo Request (type 8)
messages.note: Carries an identifier, sequence number and data.

messages.label: Echo Reply (type 0)
messages.note: Addresses are reversed, the type becomes 0, the checksum is recomputed and the data is returned unchanged.

messages.label: Datagram, TTL expires
messages.note: The gateway finds the time to live is zero and must discard the datagram.

messages.label: Time Exceeded (type 11, code 0)
messages.note: The reply carries the original IP header plus 64 bits of data, so the source can match it.
